title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 93
paragraphs: To this man's father, Euenios, this happened. At Apollonia there are sheep sacred to the Sun which by day feed by a river running from Mount Lakmon through the land of Apollonia to the sea near the harbor of Oricos; by night they are watched by men chosen for the purpose, who are the most highly regarded citizens for wealth and noble birth, each man having charge of them for a year. For the people of Apollonia set great store by these sheep because of an oracle, and they are folded in a cave at some distance from the city. At the time of which I speak, this Euenios was keeping watch over them, having been chosen for the task. It happened one night that he fell asleep during his watch, and wolves came into the cave and killed about sixty of the sheep. When he noticed this, he kept it secret, telling no one, meaning to buy others and substitute them for those killed. It was discovered, however, by the people of Apollonia, and when they were informed they brought him to court and condemned him to be deprived of his eyesight for having fallen asleep on watch. But once they had blinded Euenios, their flocks immediately ceased to bring forth young and their land to bear crops as before. Prophecies were uttered to them both at Dodona and at Delphi, when they asked the prophets the cause of the evil they were suffering, and they told them they had acted unjustly in depriving Euenios the watcher of the sacred sheep of his sight — for the gods of whom they inquired had themselves sent the wolves to attack the sheep; and they would not cease to take vengeance for him until the men of Apollonia paid Euenios such satisfaction as he himself should choose and deem sufficient. This being fulfilled, the gods would give Euenios a gift of such a kind that many men would think him happy in possessing it.
